The primitives establish a hierarchical approach: first, localize and isolate relevant objects to reduce input complexity; second, optimize computational load through targeted processing rather than full-frame analysis; third, scale this solution to multi-device environments without sacrificing temporal coherence. These operations form a dual structure where object localization acts as a preprocessor to enable efficient downstream inference. Failure modes include misidentification due to occlusion or dynamic scene changes, and performance degradation under high-density object scenarios. The system's robustness depends on adaptive thresholds and modular design principles that allow graceful degradation.
